items.title: fix(server): keep inferred types portable without baseUrl
items.body:
Closes #6998

## 🎯 Changes

Bug fix.

Since `@trpc/server` moved to bundled declarations, most shared type declarations are emitted into a hashed chunk (`dist/unstable-core-do-not-import-<hash>.d.{mts,cts}`) that isn't part of the package `exports`. The public entrypoints (e.g. `@trpc/server`) import that chunk directly, so the public `@trpc/server/unstable-core-do-not-import` entrypoint, which exists so TypeScript can name these types, is never loaded unless the consumer imports it.

As a result, when a consumer emits declarations and an inferred type references something that isn't re-exported from `@trpc/server` (e.g. `ErrorFormatterOptions` from an `errorFormatter`, or `TrackedData` from a subscription yielding `tracked()`), TypeScript reports TS2742 (TS 5.x) / TS2883 (TS 6/7). With `baseUrl` set, TypeScript instead silently emits `import("node_modules/@trpc/server/dist/unstable-core-do-not-import-<hash>.mjs").<minified>`, which is why removing `baseUrl` (or using tsgo, which no longer supports it) surfaces the error.

This adds a tsdown `footer` that appends a side-effect import of the public `./unstable-core-do-not-import.{mjs,cjs}` declaration entrypoint to the hashed chunk. Whenever the chunk is part of a program, the public entrypoint is too, and TypeScript names these types via `@trpc/server/unstable-core-do-not-import`. No runtime code changes; only the two hashed declaration chunks gain one line. (Unlike #7346, which rewrote hashed import paths after the build, this works with the current tsdown output naming.)

Regression coverage: `examples/.test/internal-types-export` now includes `src/server-only-inferred-types.ts` in its server-only build (which doesn't pull in `@trpc/client`). It fails with TS2742 before this change and passes after it.

Also verified with a packed tarball and a consumer without `baseUrl` on TypeScript 5.9, 6.0 and 7.0 (nodenext ESM, nodenext CJS and bundler resolution).

items.title: fix(server): match content-type header case-insensitively
items.body:
## Changes

Bug fix. The server picks its content-type handler with a case-sensitive `startsWith` check, so a request sent with `Content-Type: Application/JSON` is rejected with 415 UNSUPPORTED_MEDIA_TYPE, even though media type names are case-insensitive (RFC 9110, section 8.3.1). This adds a small `hasContentType` helper in `contentType.ts` that lowercases the header before matching, and uses it for the JSON, `multipart/form-data` and `application/octet-stream` handlers.

items.body: ## Why - If `httpLink` is given `headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' }`, every mutation fails with 415 `Unsupported content-type "application/json, application/json`. - The link adds its own lower-case `content-type`, then spreads the caller's headers over it. That changes the keys a custom `fetch` receives, so I kept the caller's headers as they are. ## Testing - New test in `contentTypeHeaders.test.ts` that sets `Content-Type` on `httpLink` and runs a mutation. items.title: fix(react-query): usable proxy type for createTRPCReact<AnyTRPCRouter>
items.body:
`createTRPCReact<AnyTRPCRouter>()` produces a union of false `IntersectionError` strings ("collides with a built-in method") instead of a usable proxy type (#6721).

`ProtectedIntersection<TType, TWith>` reports a collision when `keyof TType & keyof TWith` is not `never`. For `AnyTRPCRouter`, `keyof TWith` collapses to the bare `string` index signature, so `string & 'useContext'` is not `never` and every built-in key is flagged as colliding.

This guards the type: when `keyof TWith` is (or includes) the bare `string` index signature, it returns the plain intersection instead of the error. A concrete key colliding with a wide index signature is not constructible in TypeScript (an index signature collapses `keyof` to `string`), so the guard is exhaustive.

Added a regression type test. It fails to typecheck without the fix and passes with it. All packages typecheck, full vitest green, the existing collision-regression test is unchanged and still passes.

Closes #6721

### GitHub Vulnerability Alerts

#### [CVE-2026-33732](https://redirect.github.com/h3js/h3/security/advisories/GHSA-p36q-q72m-gchr)

## Summary

A pathname parsing discrepancy in srvx's `FastURL` allows middleware bypass on the Node.js adapter when a raw HTTP request uses an absolute URI with a non-standard scheme (e.g. `file://`).

## Details

When Node.js receives an absolute URI in the request line (e.g. `GET file://hehe?/internal/run HTTP/1.1`), `req.url` is set verbatim to `file://hehe?/internal/run`. Since this doesn't start with `/`, `NodeRequestURL` passes it directly to `FastURL` as a string, which stores it in `#href` for lazy manual parsing.

`FastURL#getPos()` locates the pathname by finding `://` then scanning for the next `/` — but this fails for URLs like `file://hehe?/internal/run` where a `?` appears before the first `/` after the authority. The manual parser extracts pathname as `/internal/run`, while native `URL` correctly parses it as pathname `/` with search `?/internal/run`.

This discrepancy means the router (using the fast-path) matches `/internal/run`, but if any middleware triggers a deopt to native `URL` (e.g. by accessing `hostname`), subsequent middleware sees a different pathname — bypassing route-based middleware guards.

This is a bypass of [CVE-2026-33131](https://redirect.github.com/h3js/h3/security/advisories/GHSA-3vj8-jmxq-cgj5).

## Impact

Route-based middleware (auth guards, rate limiters, etc.) can be bypassed on the Node.js adapter when a prior middleware triggers `FastURL` deopt. Requires sending a raw HTTP request (not possible from browsers).

## Fix

srvx `FastURL` constructor now deopts to native `URL` for any string not starting with `/`, ensuring consistent pathname resolution.

items.title: fix: sync the lockfile on release, fix canary pins, CLI bins and published types
items.body:
## Why

Prompted by [ghiscoding's list of lerna-lite extras](https://github.com/lerna-lite/lerna-lite/pull/1433#issuecomment-6483313122). Comparing our releases before and after the lerna-lite switch turned up these problems:

- **`main` CI is red.** Since the `v11.22.1` release commit, `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` fails with `ERR_PNPM_OUTDATED_LOCKFILE` ([run](https://github.com/trpc/trpc/actions/runs/40786499219)). Unrelated PRs fail for the same reason, e.g. #7747 fails 3 jobs.
  - Each release bumps the `@trpc/*` versions in every `package.json`, but `pnpm-lock.yaml` still records the old ones.
  - Old lerna re-synced the lockfile and put it in every release commit (`v11.17.0`–`v11.21.0`). lerna-lite doesn't, so the switch broke this.
- **Canaries point at the last stable release.** `@trpc/client@canary` has peer `@trpc/server: 11.21.1`, so installing the canaries together fails with `ERESOLVE`. Cause: our `prepack` hook (`scripts/version.ts`) strips the prerelease suffix from every `@trpc/*` pin.
- **`npx @trpc/upgrade` and `trpc-openapi` don't run.** Since `11.19.0`, `bin` points at `.js` files, but tsdown 0.23.0 builds `.mjs`. npm skips the missing links.
- **Our type declarations break consumers who type-check them** (`skipLibCheck: false`):
  - Every `@trpc/client` user needs `@types/ws`, because client imports `Encoder` from the server's ws adapter.
  - The server ws adapter's types are broken against `@types/ws` 8.18, which added ESM types.
  - `next` deep imports don't resolve for ESM consumers using `nodenext`.
  - The server adapters import `next`, `fastify`, `express`, `ws` and `aws-lambda` types without declaring them.
  - `@trpc/openapi/heyapi`'s CJS types fail on TypeScript 5.7, because `@hey-api/openapi-ts` is ESM-only.
- **Nothing caught this, because the build fails silently.** An unresolved type becomes `any` and the build still passes.

## What

- **Release tooling**
  - `lerna.json`: `syncWorkspaceLock` re-syncs the lockfile in the release commit, as old lerna did.
  - `lerna.json`: `exact` keeps lerna-lite's version bumps exact, as old lerna did. Without it the bumps become `^11.x.y`, then `version.ts` re-pins them and the lockfile is stale again.
  - `pnpm-lock.yaml`: fix the 15 stale workspace specifiers, which turns `main` green.
  - `scripts/version.ts`: pin each `@trpc/*` dep to that package's real version. Stable releases are unchanged (openapi keeps `-alpha` on stable deps). Canaries now depend on each other.
- **Bins:** `@trpc/upgrade` and `@trpc/openapi` point at `dist/*.mjs`.
- **Declarations** (runtime JS is byte-identical):
  - client: import `Encoder` from `@trpc/server/unstable-core-do-not-import`, which now re-exports it from the ws-free `wsEncoder`.
  - server ws adapter: import `WebSocket` and `WebSocketServer` from `ws` by name, which works with both old and new `@types/ws`.
  - server and next: add `.js` to type-only deep imports from `next`. Runtime imports are unchanged.
  - openapi: raise the `typescript` peer from `>=5.7.2 <7` to `>=5.8.2 <7`. 5.8.2 is the first release that lets the CJS types reference the ESM-only `@hey-api/openapi-ts`.
  - server: add optional peers `next`, `fastify`, `@types/express`, `@types/ws` and `@types/aws-lambda`. Ranges are `*`: npm rejects an installed optional peer that is outside its range, so narrower ranges would break existing users' installs.
- **New CI job `verify-packed`** (`scripts/verify-packed.ts`): packs every package, then checks it the way a consumer would.
  - Every `bin`, `exports` and `types` target is in the tarball, and every `bin` has a shebang.
  - No `catalog:` or `workspace:` specifiers end up in dependencies.
  - The tarballs install together with npm, which enforces peers.

items.title: fix(server): accept generic node-http handler options without casting
items.body:
Confidence: high — the declaration output only changes intersection order, user-facing `createContext` behaviour is pinned by type tests that also pass on main's types, and CI is green apart from a Bun job that failed while installing pnpm (`ERR_PNPM_PNPM_ENGINE_IDENTITY_UNVERIFIABLE`, an infra flake). Fixes #6057 ## Root cause When TypeScript spreads an object whose type is an intersection containing an unresolved generic member, it keeps the intersection and merges the new properties into the trailing plain-object member. `NodeHTTPHandlerOptions` was `HTTPBaseHandlerOptions & NodeHTTPCreateContextOption (conditional on TRouter) & { middleware?, maxBodySize? }`. So in a generic adapter, `{ ...opts, req, res, path }` became `HTTPBaseHandlerOptions & PartialIf<…> & { middleware?, maxBodySize?, req, res, path }`, with a fresh literal as the last member. TypeScript wouldn't accept that member for the target's own `{ middleware?, maxBodySize? }` member, so the call failed with TS2345. The same spread typechecks if you assign it to a variable first. That is why `createExpressMiddleware` and `createNextApiHandler` spread `opts as any`. ## Fix - Move `NodeHTTPCreateContextOption` to the end of the `NodeHTTPHandlerOptions` intersection, with a short comment on why the order matters. The concrete `{ middleware?, maxBodySize? }` member then survives the spread unchanged, and the new `req`/`res`/`path` properties form their own member matching `NodeHTTPRequestHandlerOptions`. This also works when an adapter adds its own trailing options, e.g. `NodeHTTPHandlerOptions<…> & { basePath?: string }`. - Remove the `opts as any` casts in the `express`, `next` and `standalone` adapters. - No change to what users can or must pass: `createContext` is still required when the router context has required fields, and optional when it is empty. The only change in the published `.d.ts` is the member order of `NodeHTTPHandlerOptions`. ## Tests - `packages/tests/server/regression/issue-6057-node-http-handler-opts-types.test.ts`: generic forwarding to `nodeHTTPRequestHandler` without a cast, with and without extra adapter options. It also covers `createContext` on the custom adapter, `createHTTPHandler`, `createExpressMiddleware` and `createNextApiHandler`: allowed to be omitted for an empty context, required (`@ts-expect-error`) for a context with required fields, and checked against the context return type. - `pnpm typecheck-packages` passes, and the examples that use these adapters typecheck. - Adapter runtime tests pass: standalone, standalone http2, express, next, fastify and node-http. - Built `packages/server` on main and on this branch and diffed the `.d.cts`/`.d.mts` output: the only change is the intersection order of `NodeHTTPHandlerOptions`.

items.title: fix(react-query): allow useQueries callbacks that return a union of tuple lengths
items.body:
Closes #6188

## The bug

A `useQueries` callback that returns different tuple lengths from different branches fails to type-check:

```
Argument of type '(t: UseQueriesProcedureRecord<...>) => [] | [...]'
is not assignable to parameter of type '(t: UseQueriesProcedureRecord<...>) => readonly []'.
  Type '[...]' is not assignable to type 'readonly []'.
    Source has 1 element(s) but target allows only 0.
```

This is **types-only**. All five reproduction variants, including `useSuspenseQueries`, pass at runtime; only the types fail. I confirmed this is not a runtime gap.

## Root cause

`packages/react-query/src/internals/useQueries.ts:198` gives the callback a contextual return type of `readonly [...QueriesOptions<TQueryOptions>]`. TypeScript cannot infer `TQueryOptions` through a **tuple spread from a union source**. A callback with two `return` branches has a union return type (`[] | [Opts]`), so inference collapsed `TQueryOptions` to `[]` and the non-empty branch was rejected.

Not caused by the `combine` option (#6377) — I verified it still reproduces with that reverted.

## Why an additive overload rather than a rewrite

I tried seven candidate fixes in a standalone model, then each in the real repo against the typecheck. **Every single-signature rewrite traded something away:**

- dropping the spread loses tuple precision
- adding a `readonly` conditional breaks the existing `results[0].data === 'foo'` assertions
- a mapped type breaks readonly support

So I used a **second call signature** instead:

1. The original signature, **byte-for-byte unchanged**, listed **first** — every existing caller keeps identical inference, because overload resolution tries this one first.
2. A new signature that infers the options array directly (`TQueries extends readonly UseQueryOptionsForUseQueries<any, any, any, any>[]`) and matches only the callbacks the first one rejects.

Verified no regression: all pre-existing `expectTypeOf` assertions pass unchanged, and I added guards for `combine` and for pre-typed `readonly` tuples/arrays.

## Tests

Three tests in `test/useQueries.test.tsx`, following the repo's `// regression https://github.com/trpc/trpc/issues/NNNN` convention: empty-array-conditional, empty-array-first plus varying tuple lengths, and readonly-options acceptance.

Each confirmed to fail without the source change (7 type errors) and pass with it.

## Verification

| command | result |
|---|---|
| `pnpm --filter @trpc/react-query typecheck` | 0 errors |
| `pnpm --filter @trpc/next typecheck` | 0 errors |
| `pnpm --filter @trpc/tests typecheck` | 0 errors |
| `pnpm vitest run packages/react-query` | 50 files, **204 passed**, no test changed behaviour |
| `lint` | clean |
| `prettier --check` | clean |

`3 files changed, +145/-15`. An early baseline run showed 9 `TS2307: Cannot find module` errors in `packages/next`; that was a partially-installed `node_modules` from a first install, resolved by re-running the install — not a pre-existing repo failure.

No changeset: tRPC removed changesets in `e599c2444` (Jan 2024) and uses `release-manual.yml`.

## Two things for you

1. **The same bug exists in `TRPCUseSuspenseQueries`** (around line 220 pre-fix) — repro case E confirms `useSuspenseQueries` fails identically. I scoped the change to `useQueries` because that is what the issue reports, but the fix very likely applies verbatim. Happy to extend it if you would rather land both together, or leave it for a follow-up.
2. The `t: any` annotation I added in `createHooksInternal.tsx:700` is looser than ideal. `no-explicit-any` is off in this repo and the file already uses `any` extensively, so it will not trip lint, but flagging it since it is technically a small loss of type safety at that one call site.

First-time contributor, apologies if I've missed a convention.

  * Preserved support for readonly tuple and array query options, including result combination callbacks.
  * Query results now accurately reflect potentially missing positions with `undefined`, improving type safety for conditional query lists.

items.title: fix(server): register keepalive once per websocket connection
items.body:
## Summary

`fastifyTRPCPlugin` registered keepalive twice for every WebSocket connection.

It calls `getWSConnectionHandler` to build its `onConnection` handler, and that handler [already registers keepalive](https://github.com/trpc/trpc/blob/main/packages/server/src/adapters/ws.ts#L124-L126) when `opts.keepAlive?.enabled` is set. The plugin then called `handleKeepAlive(socket, …)` again straight after invoking it, so each socket ended up with two ping intervals and two pong-wait timers.

## Why it matters beyond the doubled PING

@01101101 reported the duplicate PING traffic in #7502. There is a second consequence worth noting: each `handleKeepAlive` closure clears only *its own* `ping`/`timeout` handles on an incoming message. With two registrations, a client's message resets one pair while the other pong-wait timer keeps running, so a healthy connection can be terminated by the timer belonging to the registration that did not see the reset.

## The fix

Removed the plugin-level call rather than the one in `getWSConnectionHandler`. Every adapter goes through that shared handler, so keepalive belongs there, and `grep` confirms no other adapter registers it separately — the fastify plugin was the only place doing it twice.

## Test

`packages/tests/server/adapters/fastify.test.ts` gains a regression test that starts the plugin with `keepAlive` enabled, opens a raw `ws` connection and counts the `PING` messages over one and a half intervals.

I checked that it actually catches the bug rather than merely passing: with the fix reverted it fails with `expected 2 to be 1`, and passes with the fix. The whole file is 17/17 green.

One implementation note for reviewers: keepalive is sent as a `'PING'` **text message**, not a protocol-level ping frame, so the test listens on `message` rather than the `ping` event.

The test harness needed a small addition — `ServerOptions` now accepts `keepAlive`, forwarded into `trpcOptions` — since there was no existing way to enable it for the fastify adapter.

## Checklist

- [x] The fix is covered by a test that fails without it
- [x] `vitest run packages/tests/server/adapters/fastify.test.ts` passes (17/17)
- [x] `prettier` clean
- [x] Links the issue with a closing keyword: Closes #7502

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **New Features**
  * Added support for configuring WebSocket keepalive behavior and the experimental encoder through the Fastify adapter.
  * Added an option to disable automatic pong handling for WebSocket connections.

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Prevented duplicate keepalive handling that could cause repeated ping messages.

* **Tests**
  * Added coverage verifying a single ping is sent per configured interval and checking the WebSocket option types.
<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->


## Maintainer follow-up

Pushed 1995e3054d on top of this branch to close a typing gap the new test ran into:

- `FastifyTRPCPluginOptions['trpcOptions']` didn't declare `keepAlive`, even though the plugin forwards `trpcOptions` to `getWSConnectionHandler`, which honours it. `trpcOptions` now also accepts `Pick<WSSHandlerOptions<TRouter>, 'keepAlive' | 'dangerouslyDisablePong' | 'experimental_encoder'>`, which is the set of WebSocket options the connection handler reads. Those fields are only used when `useWSS` is enabled. There's no runtime change.
- The test harness no longer needs the `as FastifyTRPCPluginOptions<AppRouter>['trpcOptions']` cast. `keepAlive` is passed in the `satisfies`-checked `trpcOptions` literal, and a type-level test checks that the three fields match `WSSHandlerOptions`. Without the type change, `@trpc/tests` typecheck fails with `TS2353: 'keepAlive' does not exist in type 'FastifyHandlerOptions<...>'`.

Thanks @pri12ya871 for the fix and the regression test!

items.title: build(deps): upgrade eslint to v10
items.body:
Layer 5 of a stacked dependency upgrade. Stacked on #7575.

| package | from | to |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `eslint` | ^9.26.0 | **^10.10.0** |
| `typescript-eslint` | ^8.32 | ^8.70.0 |
| `eslint-plugin-unicorn` | 64.0.0 | ^74.0.0 |
| `eslint-plugin-react-hooks` | **6.0.0-rc.1** | ^7.1.1 |
| `@eslint/compat` | ^2.0.0 | ^2.1.1 |

`eslint-plugin-react` stays at 7.37.5 — there's no newer release. Note this also gets us off a release-candidate prerelease of `eslint-plugin-react-hooks`.

### Config migration
- **`reactHooks.configs.recommended` is eslintrc-shaped again in v7** and makes ESLint 10 fail outright (`A config object has a "plugins" key defined as an array of strings`). The flat config moved to `configs.flat.recommended`. Same fix applied to the two example configs that wire this up themselves.
- **`react-hooks/react-compiler` no longer exists.** v7 split it into ~14 granular rules (`purity`, `immutability`, `refs`, `set-state-in-effect`, `use-memo`, …) that `flat.recommended` enables. The rule entry and two stale `eslint-disable` comments referencing it are removed.
- **`unicorn/filename-case` gets `checkDirectories: false`.** unicorn 74 started checking directory names and flagged deliberate ones (`__tests__`, `aws-lambda`, `node-http`, `app-dir`). This keeps the rule scoped to filenames, as before.
- **`max-params` now counts parameters of function _types_.** The single hit is `setQueriesData`, which mirrors TanStack Query's own 4-parameter signature, so it takes a targeted disable.

### ⚠️ Five new React Compiler rules are switched off with a Todo
`react-hooks/refs`, `immutability`, `set-state-in-effect`, `use-memo` and `preserve-manual-memoization` flag **32 real findings** — `subscriptionOptions` mutating refs during render, several components calling `setState` synchronously inside an effect. That's a genuine refactor of shipped code and belongs in its own PR rather than a dependency bump, so they're disabled with a comment pointing at the work. **Everything else v7 added stays on.** Happy to split those fixes out if you'd like them tracked in an issue.

### Real bugs the new rules found
- **`sse.test.ts` had `await Promise.all([await a, await b])`** — the inner awaits ran the two operations sequentially, so the `error` listener was only registered *after* the server had already restarted. A latent flake, caught by `await-thenable`.
- **`getFetch` now returns `fetch` bound to its global.** It was already handing back an unbound method; the old `as FetchEsque` assertion just hid that from `unbound-method`. An unbound `fetch` throws `Illegal invocation` in some engines. The guards use `typeof` instead of the `isFunction` helper, which is no longer needed.
- Two optional-chain simplifications, plus dead imports/aliases left behind by `--fix`.

### Two `--fix` results were reverted
`--fix` removed two assertions that `no-unnecessary-type-assertion` considered redundant but which were **load-bearing for inference** — typechecking broke:
- `as ActionContext` in `create-action-hook.tsx` — without it `innerInput` became implicitly `any`. Now an explicit annotation, which is what was meant all along.
- `yield 1 as number` in `streaming.test.ts` (×3) — it deliberately widens the yield type; removing it narrowed the union to `1 | 2 | 3` and broke a downstream assertion. Restored with a note.

### Verification
`pnpm lint` is clean across all 42 workspaces. `pnpm build`, `typecheck-packages`, `typecheck-www`, `monotest-build` and `manypkg check` pass; `pnpm test` is 1130/1131 with only the pre-existing `httpSubscriptionLink.memory.test.ts` WeakRef/GC failure.

items.title: feat(examples): refresh tanstack-start-sse-chat with @shared/ui
items.body:
## Why - `tanstack-start-sse-chat` (Vercel project `tanstack-start-sse-chat`, sse.trpc.io) shows tRPC subscriptions over Server-sent Events on TanStack Start. It ran on Tailwind v3 with its own shadcn copies, Headless UI and Heroicons, and the landing page was a bare list of channels. - This is part of the examples UI refresh, which covers the examples that have a Vercel deployment. - **Stacking:** this PR is stacked on #7795 (next-app-dir), the top of the refresh stack: #7786 → #7789 → #7792 → #7794 → #7795 → this PR. It's no longer stacked on #7759 (query handles); the diff is only the UI refresh against the example as it is on `main`. #7759 also changes `chat.tsx`, `$channelId.tsx` and `index.tsx`, so it will conflict with this PR; that gets resolved after the refresh PRs merge. ## What - **Styling:** Tailwind v4 (`@tailwindcss/vite`) with `@shared/ui/theme.css`, which follows the system's light or dark setting. - Removed: `tailwind.config.ts`, `postcss.config.js`, and `src/components/{avatar,button,dialog,input}.tsx`. - Dropped dependencies: `@headlessui/react`, `@heroicons/react`, `@radix-ui/react-slot`, `class-variance-authority` and `tailwind-merge`. - **Layout:** a header with the logo and a Source link, and a "Not found" empty state with a way back. - **Home:** a hero, a "How it works" card (EventStream requests, `post.onAdd`, `channel.whoIsTyping`), and a Channels card. The card has a "New channel" button, or Sign in when signed out, and lists channels as items. - **Channel page:** - A sidebar with the channels and the signed-in user, plus a skeleton while loading. - A header with the channel name and the subscription state as a badge: Connecting, Reconnecting, Live, or Disconnected with a "Try again" button that calls `subscription.reset()`. - Messages use `Message`/`Bubble` rows with avatars, the author and the time. - The composer shows an error alert instead of `alert()`, and a spinner while sending. - Under the composer: who's typing. - **New channel:** a Base UI dialog with a labelled field, browser validation for the 2-character minimum, an error alert, and a spinner while creating. - **Typing fix:** `isTyping` is now sent when the composer is focused by `autoFocus` before hydration. Before, `onFocus` never fired, so nobody showed as typing until you clicked away and back. The bug is on `main` too. - **Data loading is unchanged from `main`:** loaders prefetch `channelListQuery`/`postListQuery` from `~/queries`, and `Chat` takes `channelId`. "Load more" keeps `main`'s `hasNextPage`/`isFetchingNextPage` logic, restyled (outline button with a spinner); #7759 replaces it with a `fetchStatus` switch. - **Dependency setup:** `@shared/ui` is injected, as in the Next examples, so it shares the example's React. - In dev, `ssr.noExternal` includes `@shared/ui`, because it's TypeScript source. - `optimizeDeps.include` prebundles the Base UI entries it uses. Vite neither prebundles an injected `.tsx` package nor discovers its dependencies, and Base UI's CommonJS `use-sync-external-store` fails unbundled. - **Rules followed:** mutations are named (`createChannel`, `addPost`); tRPC usage is unchanged. The one boolean flag left is `main`'s `isFetchingNextPage` in Load more, kept so this PR doesn't overlap #7759. | | Before (light) | Before (dark) | After (light) | After (dark) | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Home, signed out | ![Home signed out before, light](https://cursor.com/artifacts/c/art-efef4296-ae73-4431-a3e1-f960982b4f7d) | ![Home signed out before, dark](https://cursor.com/artifacts/c/art-838e7696-6906-4772-81db-d8529ee9d260) | ![Home signed out after, light](https://cursor.com/artifacts/c/art-6c7ff5fd-0935-4ad6-ba9f-ac137d8eb721) | ![Home signed out after, dark](https://cursor.com/artifacts/c/art-5d64fa16-c7dc-47b3-908f-39cc2cd2f926) | | Home, signed in | ![Home before, light](https://cursor.com/artifacts/c/art-4724ab5a-1515-44c5-8ba6-3b4a0479a1da) | ![Home before, dark](https://cursor.com/artifacts/c/art-bdeaf6f7-c297-4ca8-b7f3-fc60afa1a739) | ![Home after, light](https://cursor.com/artifacts/c/art-b0fad41a-5b04-4c71-b164-1034e43b0f5f) | ![Home after, dark](https://cursor.com/artifacts/c/art-e2036517-0faf-4e14-9ee2-b1881b71d95f) | | Channel, another user typing | ![Channel before, light](https://cursor.com/artifacts/c/art-e40e0f0e-692d-4520-924d-7f3229ebdcd1) | ![Channel before, dark](https://cursor.com/artifacts/c/art-5f1efbac-ad86-479a-96e3-a26f337f1df2) | ![Channel after, light](https://cursor.com/artifacts/c/art-eb210028-2b89-4b9f-828f-935d118d8a87) | ![Channel after, dark](https://cursor.com/artifacts/c/art-fd838e38-1378-4ab1-831c-23452b3ea174) | | New channel dialog | | | ![Dialog after, light](https://cursor.com/artifacts/c/art-6ab4ca6c-583e-4670-a8e9-2a7fa3698a97) | ![Dialog after, dark](https://cursor.com/artifacts/c/art-90f44dd1-ff5f-4745-827d-33fffef9295a) | ## Links - TanStack Start SSE chat preview: [Home](https://tanstack-start-sse-chat-git-cursor-tanstack-start-s-4889ff-trpc.vercel.app/), showing the hero, "How it works" and the channel list. Open a channel to see the chat, and sign in to post or create a channel. ## Alternatives considered - **Stay stacked on #7759.** That avoided conflicts on `chat.tsx`, `$channelId.tsx` and `index.tsx`, but tied the refresh to the query-handles API. Stacking on the refresh instead keeps this PR's diff to UI only. - **Not injecting `@shared/ui`; use `resolve.dedupe` for React instead.** In dev SSR, Base UI stays external and Node resolves it to the workspace's React 19.3, a second React. Injecting keeps one React everywhere, as in the Next examples. - **`optimizeDeps.include: ['@shared/ui/components/*']`.** Vite can't prebundle a package whose entries are `.tsx`, so the Base UI entries are listed instead. ## Testing - `pnpm build`, with `AUTH_SECRET` and a local Postgres `DATABASE_URL`, passes; `pnpm dev` has no console errors on `/` or a channel. - `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm lint` and `oxfmt --check` pass on the changed files. - In the browser, with two signed-in users: - posting shows up live for the other user; - "KATT is typing..." shows while KATT types, without clicking away first; - creating a channel navigates to it; - a 1-character name is blocked by the field; - signed out, the composer offers Sign in; - every page checked in light and dark. - **Standalone:** #7786's transform (now below this PR in the stack) copies the 17 components it uses into `src/shared-ui/`. The copy installs outside the workspace, `pnpm build` passes (client and SSR), and `node .output/server/index.mjs` serves `/` and a channel. - The lockfile only changes this example's entries. This example's E2E job is commented out in `main.yml`.
  
--- Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need. ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **New Features** * Refreshed the chat example with a card-based channel browser, updated chat layout, and clearer information about live updates and reconnection. * Added signed-in and signed-out account displays, channel and not-found empty states, and loading placeholders. * Added visible connection status, retry controls, and typing indicators. * **Bug Fixes** * Channel creation now validates names, shows errors inline, and prevents duplicate submissions while processing. * Message submission errors now appear in the chat, with a loading indicator while sending.

items.body:
Closes #6864.

`abortOnUnmount` is not mentioned anywhere under `www/docs/client/tanstack-react-query/`, so there is no migration path for it. items.title: fix(openapi): drop function-valued properties from generated schemas
items.body:
Top of the dependency-upgrade stack, stacked on #7583. Added at review request on #7578.

Functions carry `ts.TypeFlags.Object`, so `isObjectType()` matched them and the generator emitted `{"type": "object"}` for a function-valued property — or `{}` when the property was optional, since `fn | undefined` is a union whose only defined member is callable.

Nothing callable survives JSON serialisation, so these shouldn't appear in the schema at all.

### The fix
- **`isFunctionType`** — true when the type has call or construct signatures.
- **`isUnserialisableType`** — extends that through unions, so an optional method (`fn | undefined`) is caught too.
- Function-valued properties are skipped entirely, **including from `required`**.
- Callable members are dropped from unions.
- A callable reaching the top-level dispatch yields an empty schema.

### How it surfaced
`nodeModulesJsDocRouter` deliberately introspects vite's `AliasOptions`. Vite 8 changed `ResolverObject.buildStart` from an `ObjectHook` union to a plain function type, and the generated document started describing a function as an object. Both of that interface's properties are callable, so it now correctly generates as a bare `{"type": "object"}` — and the committed fixture sheds **~880 lines** of schema that was describing function shapes.

### Tests
`edgeCaseRouter` gains `withFunctions` and `onlyFunctions`, covering a method, an optional method, a constructor signature, a serialisable sibling property, and an object whose properties are all callable.

Both new tests were confirmed to **fail with the generator change reverted**, so they genuinely guard the fix rather than just passing.

### Verification
`pnpm build`, `typecheck-packages`, `typecheck-www`, `monotest-build`, `lint` (42/42) and `manypkg check` pass. The openapi suite is 176/176 and the full run is 1155/1156 — only the pre-existing `httpSubscriptionLink.memory.test.ts` WeakRef/GC failure.

items.title: fix(server): correct assertIsRequestId boolean logic — non-NaN invalid types passed silently
items.body:
## Summary

`assertIsRequestId` in `parseTRPCMessage.ts` has an inverted boolean condition that only throws for `NaN`. Booleans, objects, arrays, and `undefined` all pass through silently as valid request IDs.

**Root cause**

```ts
// Before — broken: only throws when typeof obj === 'number' AND isNaN(obj)
if (
  obj !== null &&
  typeof obj === 'number' &&   // short-circuits for non-numbers
  isNaN(obj) &&
  typeof obj !== 'string'      // always true when typeof obj === 'number'
) {
  throw new Error('Invalid request id');
}
```

The original intent (PR #508) was `typeof id !== 'number' || isNaN(id)`. The condition got inverted when the type was widened to `number | string | null`.

**Fix**

```ts
// After — throws for anything that is not null, a finite number, or a string
if (
  obj !== null &&
  typeof obj !== 'string' &&
  (typeof obj !== 'number' || isNaN(obj))
) {
  throw new Error('Invalid request id');
}
```

## Previously broken (now fixed)

| Input | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `NaN` | throws | throws |
| `true` | passes silently | throws |
| `false` | passes silently | throws |
| `{}` | passes silently | throws |
| `[]` | passes silently | throws |
| `undefined` | passes silently | throws |

## Tests

Added 11 unit tests in `packages/tests/server/parseTRPCMessage.test.ts` covering all valid (`number`, `string`, `null`, `0`, `""`) and all previously-silent-invalid cases.

Fixes #7430, fixes #7450

items.title: fix(server): preserve stack and name of cross-realm error causes
items.body:
Confidence: high — small, targeted change; the regression test reproduces the bug and now passes; all error-related suites and full CI are green, with no behaviour change for plain objects or native errors. Fixes #6977 ## Root cause Errors created in another realm (`node:vm`, iframes, some bundler/APM sandboxes) fail `instanceof Error`, so `getCauseFromUnknown` wraps them in `UnknownCauseError`. That wrapper copied fields with `Object.assign`, which only copies own enumerable properties. It skips the non-enumerable own `stack` and the `name` inherited from the prototype. On top of that, `getTRPCErrorFromUnknown` only inherited the cause's stack when `cause instanceof Error`. The result: `onError` reported `cause.name === 'Error'` and a stack starting inside tRPC instead of the original frames. ## Fix - Add an `isErrorLike` type guard: `instanceof Error` or `Object.prototype.toString.call(value) === '[object Error]'`. Unlike `util.types.isNativeError`, it works cross-realm and in every runtime. - In `UnknownCauseError`, after `Object.assign`, explicitly copy `name` and `stack` (when they are strings) for error-like causes. - In `getTRPCErrorFromUnknown`, inherit the stack when the cause is error-like, not only when it's `instanceof Error`. Plain thrown objects still fail the brand check and keep their own fields exactly as before. Normal `Error` causes are untouched (still returned as-is). ## Test evidence - `packages/tests/server/regression/issue-6977-cross-realm-error-cause.test.ts`: failed before (all 4 assertions on `cause.name`, `cause.stack` and `error.stack`), passes now. - Error-related suites (19 files, 277 tests) pass: `TRPCError`, `errors`, `errorFormatting`, `procedureErrors` (server and client), regressions 3351, 4217 and 7272, and every test touching `onError` or `getTRPCErrorFromUnknown`. - `tsc` for `@trpc/server` and `@trpc/tests`, prettier and eslint are clean. - CI: all checks green, including E2E for Bun, Deno, Cloudflare Workers, Vercel Edge, and Node 20/22.

items.title: fix(server): don't hang when the node request body was already consumed
items.body:
Confidence: high — a single branch that only runs for an ended stream without `req.body` (which previously always hung); full CI green. Fixes #5534 ## Root cause `createBody` in `packages/server/src/adapters/node-http/incomingMessageToRequest.ts` only checked `req.readableEnded` when `req` had a `body` property. When another middleware drained the request stream without setting `req.body` (e.g. `@koa/bodyparser` without `patchNode`), it attached `data`/`end` listeners to a stream that had already ended, so any procedure reading its input waited forever. ## Fix When the stream has ended and `req` has no `body` property, `createBody` now returns a `ReadableStream` that errors immediately with a `TRPCError`. This is the same error-on-read approach the existing `PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE` limit uses, so only procedures that actually read the body are affected. ## Behaviour - Mutations that read input fail fast with `INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR`: "The request body has already been read by another middleware. Assign the parsed body to `req.body` so tRPC can use it". - Mutations without input still succeed. - It isn't treated as an empty body, because the input is genuinely lost. An empty body would surface as a confusing validation error, or a silent `undefined` for optional inputs. - `INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR` because this is a server misconfiguration, not a client error. The message points to the same remedy as the issue (`patchNode` / assigning `req.body`). - Unchanged: `req.body` set to `undefined` on an ended stream still yields an empty body (#7447). ## Tests - `packages/tests/server/regression/issue-5534-consumed-body-hang.test.ts`: a standalone server with a draining middleware. `ping` resolves `'pong'`; `echo('hello')` rejects with `INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR` and the message above. items.title: fix(server): resolve record values lazily in Serialize
items.body:
Closes #6997

## 🎯 Changes

Bug fix. `Serialize` reports TS2589 for a recursive JSON type whose object keys are optional, such as `Prisma.JsonValue`:

```ts
type JsonObject = { [Key in string]?: JsonValue };
interface JsonArray extends Array<JsonValue> {}
type JsonValue = string | number | boolean | JsonObject | JsonArray | null;
```

Because the keys are optional, this `JsonObject` does not match the internal `JsonValue`, so `Serialize` takes the record branch. That branch was `Record<keyof T, Serialize<T[keyof T]>>`. TypeScript resolves the type argument of `Record` at once, so `Serialize<JsonValue>` expands again and again until it hits the instantiation limit.

The record branch now uses `SerializeRecord`, a mapped type with the same result. The value type is in the template, so TypeScript resolves it only when it is used, as it already does for `SerializeObject`. `SerializeRecord` is exported with `@internal`, like `SerializeObject`. Without the export, a consumer that emits declarations gets TS4023 ("cannot be named").

Checked on main at 796700d with TypeScript 6.0.3 and 7.0.2:

- A Prisma-free repro (`Serialize<{ data: JsonValue }>`, and a router read through `inferRouterOutputs`) reports TS2589 and TS7056 on main. With this change it has no errors, and the instantiations go from 89,700 to 78,502.
- The new test in `serialize.test.ts` fails with TS2589 on main and passes with the change. All 20 tests in the file pass.
- `tsc --noEmit` passes for `server`, `client`, `react-query`, `next` and `tanstack-react-query`. ESLint and Prettier pass.
- Type-check time of `packages/server` (`tsconfig.json` and `tsconfig.benchmark.json`, 5 interleaved runs per side) did not change. The differences are within the run-to-run noise.

I found the place with whyts, a trace analyzer I maintain. On main it reports the recursive instantiation in `Serialize` (`serialize.ts:35`). Thanks to @k-ahlawat for the original repro.

items.title: chore: replace ESLint and Prettier with oxlint and oxfmt
items.body:
## Why - ESLint (with type-aware typescript-eslint) and Prettier are slow on a repo this size. - oxlint + oxfmt cover the same rules and format options, run much faster, and are what `v12` already uses. ## What Two commits. Review them apart: 1. `chore: replace ESLint and Prettier with oxlint and oxfmt`: config, deps, scripts, comments. 2. `style: format repo with oxfmt`: formatter output only (73 files). Mostly unions split one member per line, plus some import moves. **Removed** - `eslint.config.js`, `prettier.config.js`, `.prettierignore`, both starters' `eslint.config.mjs`. - `eslint`, `typescript-eslint`, `eslint-plugin-react`, `eslint-plugin-react-hooks`, `eslint-plugin-unicorn`, `eslint-config-next`, `@eslint/compat`, `prettier`, `prettier-plugin-tailwindcss` and `@ianvs/prettier-plugin-sort-imports`, removed from the catalog and from every package, example and `www`. - Dead `eslintConfig` keys in `packages/*/package.json` (flat config ignored them) and the `prettier` keys in the starters. - `.eslintcache` from `.gitignore`. **Added** - `oxlint`, `oxlint-tsgolint` (type-aware), `oxfmt` and `@oxlint/plugins`, added to the catalog. - `.oxlintrc.json`: every rule ESLint ran, with the same severities, options and per-path overrides. Type-aware linting is on. - `.oxfmtrc.json`: same Prettier options (`printWidth: 80`, `trailingComma: all`, `singleQuote`). The import order and Tailwind class sorting are ported to oxfmt's built-in `sortImports` and `sortTailwindcss`. - `tooling/oxlint-plugin` (`@tooling/oxlint-plugin`, private): local JS plugin with two rules plus RuleTester tests. Same layout as `v12`'s `next/tooling/oxlint-plugin`; no code was copied from `v12`. - Each starter (`next-prisma-starter`, `next-prisma-websockets-starter`) gets its own `.oxlintrc.json` and `.oxfmtrc.json`, so it still works when cloned alone. **Scripts, CI and editor** - `lint` scripts use `oxlint ` instead of `eslint`. `examples/.experimental/next-app-dir` used `next lint`, which only worked through the root ESLint config. It now uses `oxlint src`. - `format` is `oxfmt --check`, and `format-fix` is `oxfmt`. - `.github/workflows/lint.yml` needed no change: it calls `turbo lint -- --fix` and `format-fix`. The repo has no husky or lint-staged. - `turbo.json` global deps point at `.oxlintrc.json` and `tooling/oxlint-plugin/**`. - `scripts/entrypoints.ts` and the `@trpc/upgrade` snapshot test format with oxfmt's JS API and the root config. - `.vscode`: the oxc extension is recommended, and ESLint and Prettier are in `unwantedRecommendations`. oxc is the default formatter, with format on save and `source.fixAll.oxc`. The starters get the same. **Comments** - `eslint-disable*` became `oxlint-disable*`, with rule names renamed (`@typescript-eslint/x` → `typescript/x`, `react-hooks/x` → `react/x`). - `prettier-ignore` became `oxfmt-ignore`. - Not converted: generated files, and `packages/upgrade/test/__fixtures__`, which model user code. **Other changes needed** - `tsgolint` runs on TypeScript 7, which rejects some old options: - `moduleResolution: node` became `bundler` and `target: es5` became `es2017` in some example tsconfigs. - `esModuleInterop: false` was dropped. - Root `tsconfig.json` gets `noEmit: true`, because it uses `allowImportingTsExtensions`. - `www/tsconfig.json` sets `baseUrl: null`. - `bundler` follows each package's `exports` map. In `next-prisma-websockets-starter`, `next-auth/providers` became `next-auth/providers/index`, because next-auth 4 only exports `./providers/*`. - The two websockets examples build their server with `tsconfig.server.json`, which sets `module: commonjs`. That doesn't work with `bundler`, so those configs set `moduleResolution: node` again. tsc 5.9 still builds them, and type-aware lint only reads `tsconfig.json`. - All touched examples still typecheck. - `packages/tests/tsconfig.json` now includes `suppressActWarnings.ts`. Without it, type-aware lint fell back to the root tsconfig, which globs all of `packages/**/dist` and raced with `turbo` builds. - `www/types.d.ts`: an inner `declare const` became `const` (TS1038), because oxfmt would not parse it. - Next configs: `eslint.ignoreDuringBuilds: true`. Next only knows ESLint, and lint now runs as its own task. - 12 test files get a blank line after their header comment (`// @vitest-environment node`, file-level `oxlint-disable`, `/// `). Without it, oxfmt's import sorter carries the comment down with the first import. ### Rules with no direct oxlint equivalent | ESLint rule | What I did | | --- | --- | | `@typescript-eslint/naming-convention` (type parameters must match `^(T\|\$)([A-Z]([a-zA-Z]+))?[0-9]*$`, with a leading `_` allowed) | Local rule `trpc/type-parameter-naming`, with the same regex and the same `_` handling. `infer` types are skipped, as in ts-eslint. | | `no-restricted-syntax` (bans `Symbol.dispose` / `Symbol.asyncDispose`) | Local rule `trpc/no-symbol-dispose`, with the same message. | | `react-hooks/config`, `react-hooks/gating` | Dropped. They only check React Compiler config, which this repo doesn't set. | | `/*eslint sort-keys: "error"*/` inline in `www/og-image/utils/env.js` | Moved to a config override. oxlint does not read inline config comments. | | `eslint --cache` | Dropped. oxlint has no cache, and it doesn't need one. | | `includeIgnoreFile(.gitignore)` | Not needed: oxlint reads `.gitignore` itself. | Everything else maps 1:1. `typescript/prefer-optional-chain` is still in oxlint's nursery, but it is on and passes. **oxlint quirks I hit** - A plugin's rules only run in an override if the plugin is enabled at the top level, so `react`, `typescript` and `unicorn` are all on at the top. With `correctness` turned off, only the listed rules run, as before. - `no-restricted-imports` pattern groups don't match subpaths, so each pattern has a `/**` twin. - A pattern with `importNames` also flags side-effect imports. The `waitFor` ban uses `paths` instead. ### Formatter differences from Prettier - The old sort plugin merged duplicate imports from the same module; oxfmt doesn't. Five `@trpc/upgrade` codemod snapshots now show split `@tanstack/react-query` imports. The codemod output is unchanged; only the test's formatting of it changed. - Side-effect imports stay in place, but named imports around them may now sort past them. - `endOfLine: auto` is not supported, so line endings default to LF. The repo has no CRLF files. - oxfmt also formats TOML; Prettier didn't. Starter `migration_lock.toml` files are ignored to avoid churn. - The starters set `sortPackageJson: false`, so oxfmt doesn't reorder their `package.json`. ## Links All visible changes here are formatter output or invisible `` markers. Pages should look the same as on `main`. - Docs: [Context](https://www-git-cursor-oxlint-oxfmt-migration-441c-trpc.vercel.app/docs/server/context): `prettier-ignore-start/end` → `oxfmt-ignore-start/end`. Same in v10 docs. - Docs: [Sponsors](https://www-git-cursor-oxlint-oxfmt-migration-441c-trpc.vercel.app/docs/community/sponsors): `prettier-ignore` markers in `_sponsors.mdx` → `oxfmt-ignore`. - Docs: [Home page](https://www-git-cursor-oxlint-oxfmt-migration-441c-trpc.vercel.app/): the landing intro step 1 marker. The Twitter wall, sponsors and companies data files are regenerated by scripts that now format with oxfmt. - Next.js App Router: [Home](https://trpc-next-app-dir-git-cursor-oxlint-oxfmt-migration-441c-trpc.vercel.app/) and [Server action](https://trpc-next-app-dir-git-cursor-oxlint-oxfmt-migration-441c-trpc.vercel.app/server-action): imports reordered only. - Next.js Pages Router: [Home](https://next-prisma-starter-git-cursor-oxlint-oxfmt-migration-441c-trpc.vercel.app/): new lint and format config; app code unchanged apart from formatting. - WebSockets: [Home](https://next-prisma-websockets-starter-git-cursor-oxlint-ox-0eea8d-trpc.vercel.app/): same as above, plus `tsconfig` `moduleResolution: bundler` and the `next-auth/providers/index` type import. - TodoMVC: [All](https://examples-todomvc-git-cursor-oxlint-oxfmt-migration-441c-trpc.vercel.app/all): `next.config.js` comment and lint script only. - TanStack Start SSE chat: [Home](https://tanstack-start-sse-chat-git-cursor-oxlint-oxfmt-mig-2fee68-trpc.vercel.app/): imports reordered only. - OG image: [Docs card](https://og-image-git-cursor-oxlint-oxfmt-migration-441c-trpc.vercel.app/api/docs?input=%7B%22title%22%3A%22Context%22%2C%22description%22%3A%22Learn%20how%20to%20create%20a%20context%22%2C%22permalink%22%3A%22%2Fdocs%2Fserver%2Fcontext%22%7D): the inline `sort-keys` comment in `utils/env.js` moved to config. ## Alternatives considered - **Biome**: would need different rule names and has no type-aware linting at parity. `v12` already uses oxc. - **Keep ESLint and run oxlint alongside it**: two linters to keep in sync, and the slow type-aware ESLint pass would stay. - **Copy `v12`'s plugin as is**: not done, because this PR was asked not to copy from `v12` yet. The layout matches it, so the two can be merged later. ## Testing - `pnpm lint` (turbo, 45 workspaces): 0 errors, 0 warnings. - A cold-cache rerun of the CI autofix job: `turbo lint -- --fix`, `manypkg fix`, `format-fix` leave no diff. - `pnpm format`: clean. - `pnpm build`: passes, and `scripts/entrypoints.ts` (now using oxfmt) leaves no diff. - `pnpm typecheck-packages` (including `tooling/oxlint-plugin`) and `pnpm typecheck-www`: pass. - `turbo typecheck` on every example whose tsconfig changed: passes. - The Lambda examples fail locally with the same 26 errors on `main`'s tsconfig: hoisted `@types` clash. - The Prisma examples need `prisma generate`. - `next-prisma-websockets-starter`: `next build` and the `tsconfig.server.json` build pass. The first CI run caught the `next-auth/providers` break. - `pnpm test --watch false`: 193 files and 1380 tests pass, including 18 new RuleTester tests for the local rules. - Checked that type-aware rules actually run: a planted floating promise is reported. - Checked that each `oxlint-disable` comment is still needed: `reportUnusedDisableDirectives` reports none. - Every file oxlint lints is covered by its nearest tsconfig, so none falls back to the root tsconfig. - `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`: passes. Lockfile changes are limited to the removed and added tools. Unrelated packages keep `main`'s pinned versions: `zod` stays 4.2.1 and `@vitejs/plugin-react` stays 6.1.1.
